title: 4 Queen Sacrifices
reviewNotes: All 50 saved states and captions reviewed. This is a crowded middlegame queen-sacrifice/back-rank overload demonstration, with both pairs of rooks, queens, minors and many pawns. The illustrated fourth queen sacrifice ends in a back-rank rook mate, without a worked endgame phase. Retained as a searchable channel source outside the endgame-study queue.
transcript: Fools will resign. West players will continue playing this game. But only a true insane person would ever be able to win from this position. You see, black has back rank problems because the three pawns are blocking the king from going anywhere. And white has a lot of pressure on these rooks. And when we see pressure, we need to add more to make the opponent crumble. So, white plays queen to G4, sacrificing the queen completely. But of course, the queen cannot be taken because this would be a checkmate in two moves. And the queen cannot even step away from the defense of the rook because of the same reason. Meaning that the black queen has to stay on this diagonal. And so it does with queen to b5. But white is a madman and plays queen to c4, sacrificing the queen to both the queen and the rook. But again, neither of them can get distracted because that would allow a checkmate. So again, black has to leave the queen there and stay on this diagonal. So it simply goes back to D7. And now a wise player might simply go back and try to repeat moves here and get a draw. But not this player because white plays queen to C7, throwing the queen at black, fully aware that it cannot be taken. Now, of course, the queen can go back to B5, but white follows up with A4, trying to cover all of the squares on this diagonal. The queen has to take. And now, another brilliant move, rook to E4. And the queen is still hanging. And this time, so is the rook. Black can of course take, but this would still lead to a checkmate, meaning that the queen has to move away and go back to B5 for the third time. But now the absolutely crazy player with the white pieces takes the pawn on B7, sacrificing the queen for the fourth time. And this time, every single square on this diagonal is covered. Meaning that the black queen will either have to move away or accept our sacrifice and allow us to checkmate.
